newsitem.title: INDIA: India and Turkmenistan sign pacts to bolster trade.
newsitem.headline: India and Turkmenistan sign pacts to bolster trade.

text.p: India and Turkmenistan on Tuesday signed five agreements, including one to avoid double taxation, to boost bilateral trade, officials said.

"The convention on avoidance of double taxation seeks to provide a fresh impetus to the mutual flow of investment technology, trade and services between the two countries," a Foreign Ministry statement said.

A double taxation avoidance pact would offer attractive tax concessions to investors and businessmen of the two countries. The pact would come into force with the updating of documents by legal authorities of the two countries, it said.
The other agreements signed relate to cooperation in health and medicine, environment and forestry and art and culture.

The agreements were signed in New Delhi by ministers of the two countries in the presence of visiting Turkmenistan President Saparmurat Niyazov and Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, a ministry official told Reuters.
The two countries are also eager to jointly explore oil and natural gas fields in Turkmenistan, which has large untapped potential, officials said on Monday.
Niyazov, who arrived in New Delhi on a two-day visit has had a series of meetings with Indian leaders and officials including the President and the Prime Minister.
The foreign ministers of India, Iran and Turkmenistan signed a transit agreement last week in Tehran to facilitate cargo traffic among the three countries and to Central Asian countries.
